method: Each row is named and marked as carried in the pack, worn, or consumed; changing the item unit converts the numbers already entered so the load itself stays the same. Item weights are converted to grams with 1 g = 1 g, 1 kg = 1000 g, 1 oz = 28.349523125 g and 1 lb = 453.59237 g, and body weight with 1 kg = 1000 g or 1 lb = 453.59237 g. Base weight is the sum of the carried rows; total pack weight is base weight plus consumables, and skin-out weight is total pack weight plus worn items. Each figure is divided by body weight in grams and multiplied by 100 to give a share of body weight, so a 4900 g base on a 75 kg hiker is 6.53%. The heaviest row is the first row with the largest converted weight, and its share is taken against base weight only, shown as 0 when base weight is 0. Rows whose name and weight are both blank are ignored in the page; an item may weigh 0 to 50000 g, a list holds 1 to 100 rows, and body weight is limited to 20 to 400 kg (44 to 880 lb). A load whose rows are all zero is rejected. Values are kept unrounded until display, where grams are rounded to whole grams, kilograms and pounds to two decimals and ounces to one decimal. A pack-share above 20% is labelled a rule-of-thumb warning, not a limit. This is load arithmetic for trip planning, not medical, safety or equipment-rating advice. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Base weight counts gear carried in a pack and excludes worn items and consumables; total pack weight adds consumables and skin-out weight adds worn items.
The international avoirdupois ounce is exactly 28.349523125 grams and the international avoirdupois pound is exactly 453.59237 grams.
Backpacking guidance commonly uses a share of body weight, often about 20% for total pack weight, as a rule of thumb rather than a hard limit.
